criterion_scores.reasoning: The cap's core arithmetic (append 0.65 to the caps list, take the min, never raise a score) is implemented identically in judge_lib.py, gemini-judge.sh's jq, and quorum-merge.sh's jq — verified line-by-line and confirmed by a real positive-control re-judge (sonnet-yed236: 0.784/pass under @5 vs 0.65/flag under @6 with privacy_layer_defect=true, both rows present in the run-logs). Both structured-output schemas (Gemini responseSchema, OpenAI json schema) correctly list privacy_layer_defect in both 'required' and 'properties'. Set against that: .claude/commands/judge-build.md Step 3 — the literal orchestration instruction for BOTH seats — still names build-quality-v5.md as what to dispatch against, an unrepaired self-contradiction inside the very artifact whose stated purpose is to close this gap everywhere. Scripts' own defaults save the practical outcome today, but the harness's own instructions are not internally consistent.

All required implementation sites named in the per-artifact spec (judge_lib.score, gemini-judge.sh jq, quorum-merge.sh Claude-seat recompute, both provider schemas, seat-log.py's rubric-version fallback, the SKILL.md pointer, cross-provider-judge.md) are present and correct. Two things fall short of the artifact's own 'docs updated... parity tests added' claim: (1) judge-build.md Step 2 and Step 3 were left un-updated (stale @5 references), one of which (Step 3) names the wrong rubric file outright; (2) the parity-test net covers judge_lib.py<->gemini-judge.sh but not quorum-merge.sh's separate copy of the same arithmetic, so 'parity tests added' is true for one duplicate pair, not all.

Rubric-versioning discipline (new build-quality-v6.md file, v5 retained untouched, 'never mutate' honored) is followed correctly. SKILL.md correctly demotes v5 to 'previous' and promotes v6 to 'current' with an accurate one-paragraph delta summary. cross-provider-judge.md was fully and correctly repointed to @6 with no leftover v5 mentions. The one slip is judge-build.md's Steps 2/3, which breaks the same house convention (every doc that names the rubric version should track the live one) that the rest of this diff otherwise honors well.

Lean, single-purpose addition — one new composite cap, no new abstraction layer, no speculative surface, no resurrection of a tombstoned decision. It does perpetuate a pre-existing architectural choice (the same cap arithmetic hand-duplicated across 3 files rather than one shared source), but that pattern predates this PR and the PR does correctly extend all three existing copies rather than adding a 4th inconsistent one.

Comments are clear and locate the 'why' at the point of change (e.g. '# @6 (YED-231): a broken privacy layer fails, backstop or not'). The SKILL.md test-evidence note is honest about a real validity threat ('that seat read later git history that names the bug'), which is exactly the kind of gap-honesty the rubric rewards. Docked for: the un-mechanized quorum-merge.sh duplicate (a silent-drift risk with no test alarm), and seat-log.py promoting confidence_honesty_violation to a top-level log-row field for easy querying while privacy_layer_defect is not given the same treatment (present only nested inside cap_flags) — a minor but real asymmetry in what's easy to audit later.

defects.quote: Both score all 5 `build-quality@5` criteria (0–1 + reasoning, **defects listed first**) using `judge-system-v2.md` + `build-quality-v5.md`.
defects.why: This is Step 3 of .claude/commands/judge-build.md, the actual orchestration entry point for /judge-build — and this diff did NOT touch it (it's unchanged diff context sitting two lines above the +/- that bumped Step 4 to @6 in the same file). It still names build-quality-v5.md as the rubric BOTH seats should be dispatched against, directly contradicting Step 4 three lines later ('rubric:"build-quality@6"'), the SKILL.md 'Load first' section (correctly bumped to v6), and the per-artifact spec's own claim that 'docs updated' is part of this PR's scope. gemini-judge.sh and openai_judge.py's own --rubric defaults were correctly repointed to v6, so the actual script invocations shown in Step 3 ('bash .claude/hooks/gemini-judge.sh --artifact <path> --artifact-type <t> --calibration-set prospective', no --rubric flag) will in practice load v6 despite the stale prose — but a careless follow of Step 3's literal wording (e.g. an operator adding an explicit '--rubric .claude/evals/rubrics/build-quality-v5.md' because that's what the step says to use, or a Sonnet-seat dispatch prompt built verbatim from Step 3) would silently score the artifact against a rubric with NO privacy-layer cap at all — precisely the failure mode this whole PR exists to close (a 'first-layer' correctness defect in the judge harness itself, self-referentially).

defects.quote: | ([$raw] + (if $f.confidence_honesty_violation then [0.65] else [] end) + (if $f.density_padding then [0.65] else [] end) + (if $f.privacy_layer_defect then [0.65] else [] end) | min) as $capped
defects.why: This is quorum-merge.sh's Claude-seat self-recompute — a THIRD independent hand-written copy of the exact same cap arithmetic that also lives in judge_lib.score() (Python) and gemini-judge.sh's jq block. The diff correctly added the privacy_layer_defect term here too, so today all three are in sync. But test_judge_lib.py's parity test only extracts and checks gemini-judge.sh's jq program against judge_lib.py (by regex, at test time) — there is no equivalent extraction/parity test binding quorum-merge.sh's copy to the canonical Python arithmetic. SKILL.md's test-evidence note ('parity tests added') and the Purpose line ('wired into every scorer... with... parity tests added') read as if the sync is now mechanically guaranteed everywhere; it's only guaranteed for 2 of the 3 implementations. A future edit to one of the other two (e.g. a 4th cap added to judge_lib.py but not copy-pasted into quorum-merge.sh) would pass every existing test and silently desync the Claude seat's self-check from the harness's authoritative arithmetic.

Same file, one step earlier: Step 2 still labels the dangling-reference cap '@5' even though the file's own description line and Step 4 were bumped to @6. Low impact (the dangling-ref cap's value, 0.60, is unchanged across @3 through @6, so no behavioral drift), but it's more evidence the version bump across .claude/commands/judge-build.md was only partially propagated — exactly the two lines the diff's own hunk touched (description + Step 4's log-string), and nothing else in the file was audited for staleness.
